jobs.description:
Position Summary

AJ Residence is a family-centered provider supporting children, youth, and adults with developmental disabilities in Northern Virginia and Richmond. The organization offers residential homes and day support programs that promote independence, dignity, and community integration for the individuals and families we serve.
The Residential Program Coordinator joins the management team of AJ Residence's Northern Virginia residential homes. The Residential Program Coordinator keeps the homes running day to day: the person who makes sure that appointments happen, documentation is complete, medications are properly documented, homes are clean and well supplied, and individuals experience meaningful days in their homes and in the community.
This role requires a certain way of thinking. Each individual we serve must be known and supported as an individual, with their own health needs, preferences and goals. The Residential Program Coordinator is expected to pay attention to the whole person: to notice what is changing in someone's health or mood, to connect what happens at a medical appointment with what staff see at home, and to advocate for each individual with providers, families, and support coordinators. Compassion for this population is a requirement of the role.

Appointment Coordination

The Residential Program Coordinator is responsible for coordinating medical, dental, therapy, and other appointments for the individuals in both homes. This covers scheduling, prompt calendar entry, preparation, transportation, attendance, and follow-up on outcomes and referrals, with results communicated to the management team and carried into daily care. This function is a primary measure of performance in this role.

Documentation, Medication, and Incident Oversight

The Residential Program Coordinator reviews daily documentation and medication administration records for accuracy and completeness, reports medication concerns to the Program Director, who holds clinical authority as a Registered Nurse, and ensures records, medication counts, and storage meet DBHDS requirements. The role maintains organized individual records, supports personnel records in coordination with the management team, and tracks incident reports from occurrence through resolution.

Homes, Daily Life, and Staff Coordination

The Residential Program Coordinator conducts regular walkthroughs of both homes to check cleanliness, supplies, and individuals' grooming and daily routines, and plans community outings suited to what each person enjoys and can participate in safely. The role guides Direct Support Professionals in their daily work, coordinates coverage when callouts occur, and keeps the management team informed. The position includes a rotating weekend on-call schedule shared with the management team.

Qualifications

A minimum of two years of direct experience serving individuals with intellectual or developmental disabilities is required.
An associate degree is required; a bachelor's degree in human services, psychology, health administration, or a related field is a plus.
The right candidate demonstrates genuine compassion for this population, sound judgment, strong organization, reliable follow-through, and a desire to grow professionally in the developmental disabilities field.
Familiarity with DBHDS regulations, Medicaid waiver services, and electronic documentation systems is preferred. A valid driver's license and reliable transportation are required.

How to Apply

Submit a resume with a short note, three to five sentences, on why this role and what your two years with this population looked like, applications with the note reviewed first.

Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Streamflow Hydrologist
(Hydrogeologist 2) within the Environmental Assessment Program .

Location:

Central Region Office in Union Gap, WA .
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
This position requires field work. Mondays and Wednesdays are in office days, other days that do not involve field work can be teleworked.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by July 30, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

In this role, you will collect and process credible stream hydrology information for river systems or basins that are reliable, accurate and timely. You will possess and demonstrate the skills required to install and operate stream gages in the assigned geographical area. You will also evaluate and develop rating curves, reviewing data for completeness and overall quality and providing field support to keep stations on-line and reporting accurate information.

What You Will Do

Using sound scientific principles, select measurement points that are representative of the measurement of stream discharge.
Develop individual state discharge rating curves for each measurement site by taking flow measurements that define this relationship over the entire flow regime.
Carry out cross section measurements at individual measurement sites so that accurate calculations can confirm the stage discharge rating curves developed.
Track the change in channel cross-section over time and adjust the stage-discharge rating table.

Position Summary

AJ Residence is a family-centered provider supporting children, youth, and adults with developmental disabilities in Northern Virginia and Richmond. The organization offers residential homes and day support programs that promote independence, dignity, and community integration for the individuals and families we serve.
The Residential Program Coordinator joins the management team of AJ Residence's Northern Virginia residential homes. The Residential Program Coordinator keeps the homes running day to day: the person who makes sure that appointments happen, documentation is complete, medications are properly documented, homes are clean and well supplied, and individuals experience meaningful days in their homes and in the community.
This role requires a certain way of thinking. Each individual we serve must be known and supported as an individual, with their own health needs, preferences and goals. The Residential Program Coordinator is expected to pay attention to the whole person: to notice what is changing in someone's health or mood, to connect what happens at a medical appointment with what staff see at home, and to advocate for each individual with providers, families, and support coordinators. Compassion for this population is a requirement of the role.

Appointment Coordination

The Residential Program Coordinator is responsible for coordinating medical, dental, therapy, and other appointments for the individuals in both homes. This covers scheduling, prompt calendar entry, preparation, transportation, attendance, and follow-up on outcomes and referrals, with results communicated to the management team and carried into daily care. This function is a primary measure of performance in this role.

Documentation, Medication, and Incident Oversight

The Residential Program Coordinator reviews daily documentation and medication administration records for accuracy and completeness, reports medication concerns to the Program Director, who holds clinical authority as a Registered Nurse, and ensures records, medication counts, and storage meet DBHDS requirements. The role maintains organized individual records, supports personnel records in coordination with the management team, and tracks incident reports from occurrence through resolution.

Homes, Daily Life, and Staff Coordination

The Residential Program Coordinator conducts regular walkthroughs of both homes to check cleanliness, supplies, and individuals' grooming and daily routines, and plans community outings suited to what each person enjoys and can participate in safely. The role guides Direct Support Professionals in their daily work, coordinates coverage when callouts occur, and keeps the management team informed. The position includes a rotating weekend on-call schedule shared with the management team.

Qualifications

A minimum of two years of direct experience serving individuals with intellectual or developmental disabilities is required.
An associate degree is required; a bachelor's degree in human services, psychology, health administration, or a related field is a plus.
The right candidate demonstrates genuine compassion for this population, sound judgment, strong organization, reliable follow-through, and a desire to grow professionally in the developmental disabilities field.
Familiarity with DBHDS regulations, Medicaid waiver services, and electronic documentation systems is preferred. A valid driver's license and reliable transportation are required.

Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Streamflow Hydrologist
(Hydrogeologist 2) within the Environmental Assessment Program .

Location:

Central Region Office in Union Gap, WA .
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
This position requires field work. Mondays and Wednesdays are in office days, other days that do not involve field work can be teleworked.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by July 30, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

In this role, you will collect and process credible stream hydrology information for river systems or basins that are reliable, accurate and timely. You will possess and demonstrate the skills required to install and operate stream gages in the assigned geographical area. You will also evaluate and develop rating curves, reviewing data for completeness and overall quality and providing field support to keep stations on-line and reporting accurate information.

What You Will Do

Using sound scientific principles, select measurement points that are representative of the measurement of stream discharge.
Develop individual state discharge rating curves for each measurement site by taking flow measurements that define this relationship over the entire flow regime.
Carry out cross section measurements at individual measurement sites so that accurate calculations can confirm the stage discharge rating curves developed.
Track the change in channel cross-section over time and adjust the stage-discharge rating table.
Install, operate and maintain water stage height telemetry systems.
Download data loggers and service telemetry systems and/or making upgrades as necessary.
Act as a resource to other agencies and groups that require technical assistance in regards to stream discharge measurement.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Six years of experience and/or education as described below:

Experience
: in hydrogeology, hydrology, geology or closely allied profession

demonstrated competence in the following skill sets:

Teamwork & Collaboration – Ability to work respectfully and cooperatively with others to support shared goals and maintain productive working relationships.
Adaptability – Ability to adjust to changing field conditions, project demands, and new technologies to remain effective in varied situations.
Critical Thinking & Problem Solving – Ability to interpret information, troubleshoot issues, and make sound decisions to resolve problems and support program objectives.
Field Operations – Ability to plan, prepare for, and conduct fieldwork safely and effectively to collect accurate environmental data.
Hydrologic Measurement & Analysis - Ability to measure stream flow and channel characteristics to develop and update accurate stage-discharge rating curves.
Data Quality & Management – Ability to record, review, and maintain accurate data and notes to ensure data integrity and support scientific analyses. Ability to enter, validate, and analyze data using databases and standard office software to support accurate reporting.
Equipment & Vehicle Operation – Ability to safely operate field equipment, tools, vehicles, and/or boats to access sites and maintain monitoring stations.

Education:
involving a major study in hydrogeology, hydrology, geology or closely allied field.

a Master’s degree or higher.

Professional Conduct – Ability to maintain a calm, respectful, and professional demeanor to support a positive and inclusive work environment.
